extracted_text: A total of 134 consecutive patients with space-occupying cerebellar infarction were retrospectively analyzed. Mean age was 68.5 ± 12.3 years (range 42-89 years), with 72 male and 62 female patients.

At 90-day follow-up, functional outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Good outcome (mRS 0-2) was achieved in 56 patients (41.8%), moderate disability (mRS 3-4) in 48 patients (35.8%), and poor outcome (mRS 5-6) in 30 patients (22.4%).

Suboccipital decompressive craniectomy (SDC) was performed in 89 patients (66.4%) with a mean time from symptom onset to surgery of 28.6 ± 14.2 hours. Conservative management was pursued in 45 patients (33.6%).
Overall in-hospital mortality was 18.7% (25/134). Mortality in the SDC group was significantly lower at 12.4% (11/89) compared to 31.1% (14/45) in the conservative management group (p < 0.01).

This prospective cohort study included 78 patients with space-occupying cerebellar infarction admitted between January 2010 and December 2014. Inclusion criteria: (1) acute cerebellar infarction with mass effect, (2) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score ≥10, (3) Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score ≤13.

Post-operative complications in the SDC group included: cerebrospinal fluid leak (n=7, 12.5%), wound infection (n=4, 7.1%), hydrocephalus requiring ventriculoperitoneal shunt (n=9, 16.1%), and rebleeding (n=2, 3.6%). No cases of cerebellar necrosectomy were performed.
